title: What the model can see
intro: Context is the information supplied for a particular invocation. A file on disk is not automatically part of that input.
takeaway: Distinguish information that exists from information actually supplied to the model.

beats.text: A contract file exists in the repository. That does not mean the model has read it.
The application selects information. Only selected content enters this input.
The model receives the assembled input. It can use the supplied contract.
Context is specific to this invocation. Check what was actually included.

title: Retrieve relevant evidence
intro: The task is to fix invoice latency. Retrieval should bring in the code and contract that constrain that change, not every nearby document.
takeaway: Relevance is a selection problem. Retrieved content still needs checking for authority and applicability.

beats.text: The task is to fix invoice latency. Find evidence that constrains this change.
Retrieve the endpoint and v1 contract. They explain behavior that must remain.
Supply those records to the model input. Include where each record came from.
More material is not always more useful. Select evidence that changes the decision.

title: Preserve a constraint
intro: Existing clients expect total_cents. An optimization must keep that field. The constraint needs to be visible when the agent chooses its edit.
takeaway: State what must remain unchanged and reference the authoritative contract. The model still needs verification.

beats.text: Clients expect the field total_cents. Latency work must preserve that contract.
Include the unchanged-field requirement. Keep its contract reference with it.
The agent proposes a compatible edit. The field name stays total_cents.
A visible constraint guides the edit. A check must still verify the result.

title: Make a useful handoff
intro: A resumed task needs a concise record of the goal, important constraints, evidence and unresolved work. Summarization can lose crucial details.
takeaway: A handoff is a shorter representation, not perfect memory. Preserve references so the next session can retrieve omitted detail.

beats.text: The current session must hand work over. A vague summary can lose the contract.
Record the goal and unchanged field. Keep evidence and open questions too.
The next session receives the handoff. It can retrieve the source when needed.
Shorten incidental history first. Do not silently drop decisive constraints.

title: Verify the patch
intro: A saved compatibility fixture checks that the optimized endpoint still returns the required field. Run it against the actual changed code.
takeaway: Good context reduces ambiguity; it does not prove the result correct. Verification closes the gap.

beats.text: The patch claims to preserve compatibility. The claim still needs evidence.
Run the v1 response fixture. Check the actual response field.
The response still has total_cents. The checked contract is satisfied.
Keep the result with the patch revision. Context and verification work together.
